findings.summary: Under matched conditions (Halcyon-G7, batch size 1, 16-bit, 0.05 m voxels, 1,000 test scans), Gossamer-Seg has lower median latency (29.4 ms vs 47.8 ms), lower 90th-percentile latency (33.1 ms vs 52.6 ms), higher throughput (34.0 vs 20.9 scans/s), and lower peak memory (3.1 vs 4.6 GB) than Tumbril-3D.
findings.scope: Coldharbour-LiDAR test scans, matched re-timing conditions
findings.caveats: No statistical test reported for latency differences; these are point estimates from a single matched run.

findings.summary: Gossamer-Seg achieves slightly higher test mIoU (67.9 ± 0.3%) than Tumbril-3D (67.5 ± 0.5%), but the paired t-test (n=3 seeds) is not statistically significant (p=0.18, 95% CI [-0.46, 1.26] percentage points).
findings.caveats: Non-significant difference does not establish equivalence; small seed count.

findings.summary: Per-class IoU on selected classes shows mixed results: Gossamer-Seg is higher on car (95.1 vs 94.8), cyclist (63.4 vs 61.9), and pole (62.0 vs 61.2), but lower on pedestrian (71.8 vs 73.0) and vegetation (86.7 vs 86.9).
findings.scope: Coldharbour-LiDAR test sequences, selected classes, 3 seeds
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported for per-class differences; differences are small.

findings.summary: Gossamer-Seg has higher compute cost per scan (96.3 GFLOPs vs 81.5 GFLOPs) and more parameters (41.7 M vs 38.2 M) than Tumbril-3D, despite being faster in matched latency.
findings.scope: One average Coldharbour-LiDAR test scan, analytical compute proxies
findings.caveats: Compute proxies are analytical, not measured; higher compute does not preclude lower latency due to architectural efficiency.

findings.summary: The originally published latencies (Gossamer-Seg: 61 ms on Halcyon-G4, 32-bit, batch 1; Tumbril-3D: 48 ms on Halcyon-G7, 16-bit, batch 4) are not directly comparable due to differing hardware, precision, and batch size, and Tumbril-3D's reported latency excludes voxelisation.
findings.caveats: These numbers should not be used for head-to-head comparison; matched re-timing (T3) is the valid comparison.

passages.text: On a Halcyon-G7 accelerator with batch size 4 and half-precision arithmetic, Tumbril-3D processes a 64-beam scan in 48 ms, which we report as amortised per-scan latency excluding voxelisation.
